newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds ended lower in a market showing signs of investor interest wearing thin in the run-up to year-end.
"A lot of people are not investing. The market is quiet," one trader said.
With Swiss interest rate policy expected to remain consistent to year-end, and currency activity also fairly quiet, focus was mainly on maintaining the status quo.
The next major event for the market may be the Swiss Federal Government's bond auction. Terms are due November 26 and the auction will conclude on November 28 SWIU.

Meanwhile, the spread between German cash Bunds and Swiss Confederate bonds continued to narrow. It stood at 190 basis points YLDS3 on Wednesday, down from levels generally above 200 basis points earlier this year.
CS analyst Christian Heyden, in a recent newsletter, expected the spread to narrow to 180 basis points in the coming month as German bond prices improved, while Swiss prices remained fairly steady.
Swiss prices held fairly steady in the morning but dipped in the afternoon, with latest foreign bond issues seeing declines of 10 to 20 Swiss centimes.
Swap rates were up by roughly five basis points, but the rise was most pronounced at the short end of the curve, swap dealers said. -- Wednesday closing prices as follows:
Dec Conf futures CONFZ6 down 20 at 115.05.
Dec Comi medium-term bond COMIZ6 down 11 at 109.75
Dec Euro Swiss francs FESM6 off 11 at 97.71.
